decisions.executionNote: Board depicts a cream dog with brown ears. Begin left-arm approach to basket, keeping the right arm clear; geometry of handle will be reassessed.
The first approach was rejected before movement. Retry with much smaller increments to establish continuous elbow-up motion.
Advance left gripper toward the near-left basket edge while observing the basket's conveyor drift. Keep current horizontal orientation for handle approach.
Reduce approach increments following continuity rejection; track basket before committing to a grasp.
Basket has drifted into the right workspace. Use the right arm for the basket so the left remains available for the incoming dog target; begin a continuous forward approach.
Continue smaller right-arm increments toward the moving basket handle, raising slightly to avoid the rim. Left stays clear.
Advance right gripper toward the handle while shifting inward to the basket's anticipated position. Maintain horizontal wrist and open fingers.
Align open right fingers around the right curved section of the basket handle, following its conveyor drift.
Advance the last few centimeters around the handle, close the right gripper and begin a small test lift. Retention must be checked visually.
Test basket retention by lifting the closed right gripper 10 cm vertically. Check that the basket follows rather than relying on the gripper command.
Lift further and bring the basket slightly inward on the right side; the handle appears to have moved, so check sustained basket following and clearance.
Basket did not follow the last lift; reopen and change to an overhead handle grasp, keeping right-arm configuration continuous.
Replan from interrupted pose with smaller wrist rotation while moving above the basket; reopen fully.
Approach the basket handle from above with a gradual downward-facing wrist, compensating for conveyor drift and maintaining elbow-up continuity.
Stop rotating near the IK limit. Translate down and back at the existing oblique angle to center the handle between open fingers.
Use half-sized translations after the continuity rejection, backing away from the near-limit configuration while lowering toward the handle.
Move toward the handle's curved right section and slightly back/down, using small wrist corrections to improve the grasp rather than closing ahead of the handle.
Close at the current handle alignment, allow the grasp to settle, then test with a small upward/backward motion while checking RGB retention.
The basket is still drifting and the closed fingers are empty. Reopen and lower toward the nearer left rim/handle attachment rather than continuing an unretained lift.
Close where the nearer basket wall lies between the open fingers, then test retention with a small inward/upward movement.
The rim remains just outside the right finger. Shift the open gripper right and slightly down to straddle it, then close for another small retention test.
The basket wall is now between the fingers. Keep the grip closed and lift 10 cm while drawing inward to verify a retained basket.
No basket retention after the lift. Move the open gripper closer to the drifting near rim and substantially lower the fingertips, maintaining the current wrist configuration.
Bring the fingertip center onto the near sidewall at a lower height, tracking the rim's rightward drift, then close around the wall.
Center the near rim more deeply in the jaws, then close and follow conveyor motion without lifting until the grasp has settled.
Track the remaining visible basket rim farther right and attempt a deeper sidewall grasp. Move the left arm toward the incoming cream-and-brown dog without crossing workspaces.
Right arm is near its reach limit; retract slightly and angle the fingers toward the rim instead of extending farther. Left approaches above the identified dog.
Angle right fingertips farther toward the near basket rim while retaining reach margin. Left aligns its open jaws with the dog, not the adjacent figurine.
Lower the right fingers onto the now-visible near basket wall and close without further extension. Left lowers slightly around the dog and begins closing.
Back the right EE inward after the reach-limit rejection while adjusting its approach direction. Close the left gripper on the dog and begin a small retention test.
Left fingers closed above the dog; reopen, follow its drift, and descend more deeply around the head/body. Retract the right arm from the reach boundary as the basket has moved out of safe reach.
Allow the dog grasp to close fully before lifting it 5 cm for a visual retention check. Continue retracting the empty right arm safely.
Dog did not rise reliably. Reopen and place the left fingers farther forward and lower around its body before closing again; right retreats to a central safe posture.
Settle the deeper dog grasp and make a slow vertical retention test; continue keeping the empty right arm away from its extension limit.
The dog is still below the closed tips rather than retained. Reopen and descend substantially while tracking it, keeping the right arm stationary.
The wrist view places the dog behind the finger tips; back the left EE toward the robot while tracking rightward to put the jaws, not the housing, around it.
Dog is centered between the open jaws. Close while matching its drift, settle, then lift slowly to test retention.
The jaws again appear empty above the dog. Reopen and make a deeper body-level approach with modest forward motion, staying on the left side.
Dog body is now deep in the jaws at the lower approach height. Finish closing in place, then test with a small lift.
The dog now appears retained between the jaws. Lift it away from the conveyor and back into the left workspace, maintaining the closed grip.
